excerpt: Conductor lets you run Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode in parallel.
Each task gets its own workspace, branch, files, terminal, diff, and review path.

Pick a loadout of your favorite models to quickly switch between. It’s keyboard accessible too: change models (⌃⌘ 1-5), effort (⌘⇧/), speed (⌘⇧E) or model ordering (Tab, then space) without leaving your keyboard.
Introducing routines! You can now run your agents on a schedule or via GitHub action.
You can now create private workspaces that aren’t shared with the rest of your team.
Search file contents in your current local project or cloud workspace with ⌘⇧F.
Sign in to your Cursor subscription for cloud workspaces.
You can now edit attachments in queued messages.
Copy, save, download, or open images from chat previews, including expanded previews.
Enable Exclusive port forwarding in Settings → Ports to turn forwarding off in other workspaces whenever you turn it on in one.
PR comments and failing-check logs now load while a cloud workspace is asleep.
Use Command + Shift + N or the `...` button next to `New workspace` to create a workspace from a branch, pull request, GitHub issue, or Linear issue.
The Conductor API lets you manage cloud workspaces programmatically.
Conductor's hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) server lets ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, and other MCP clients manage your cloud workspaces.
The link opens the workspace in Conductor for any member of the organization.
Right-click the workspace and choose **Reassign to** to make a teammate responsible for it.
The agent can test your repositories, update install and setup scripts, and run builds — without asking you to confirm each step.
Checkpoints | Session/workspace | Revert code and chat state to an earlier turn
Bring your own subscriptions and keys
Sandboxes spin up in seconds, and agents keep working after you close your laptop.

Full read-write access required to all your Github account's repos. Not just code. Settings, deploy keys. The works... Zero disclosure of data practices. You are INSANE to authorize this app on anything other than throwaway code.

I was really excited to try this but this does NOT work the way I expected. I wanted a simple git worktree manager for my existing, already-checked-out repository. Instead, it requests Github permissions and clones the repo from Github... it's like Codex or Cursor Background Agents, except worse, because it's on your machine.

I have been imagining something like this would be perfect for working with Claude Code... This feels like just a nice clean simple extension of how Claude code already works that solves my most common pain points in the workflow. Anyways, excellent work!

Love the design. does it build on electron? and will it support other code agents, like gemini cli, codex, opencode ext.
